idiom_name: one struct + diesel::table! module per table; enum for mixed results
implementation_notes: Rust has no inheritance, so the mapping arrives as plain per-table types: Diesel's table! macro generates a module per table and one struct per table derives Queryable/Insertable for it, with the shared columns either repeated or embedded through #[diesel(embed)] in a base struct; sqlx's query_as! gives the same shape from checked SQL. Mixed collections are expressed with an enum whose variants carry the concrete structs, filled from a UNION ALL query or one query per table. Composition plus enum dispatch is how Rust models the hierarchy, so choose this mapping when leaf-scoped access dominates and you want no join, not as an attempt to reproduce a class hierarchy.
pitfalls: Diesel derives are per table: a shared column change must be made in every table! block, struct and migration, and the compiler will not connect them.
Keys are generated per table, so two tables with their own sequences produce colliding ids; use one sequence (PostgreSQL) or UUIDs before treating rows as one hierarchy.
A UNION ALL returning heterogeneous columns needs every branch cast to a common type with NULL padding, and sqlx's compile-time checks reject any drift.
